mem0.rationale: Durable identity + platform fact. Useful for path defaults, OS-specific guidance.

mem0.rationale: Sets expectation that Claude should be proactive and execute, not just advise.

mem0.text: Greg adopted a four-layer memory protocol in May 2026: Hot = SESSION-STATE.md (project root, survives compaction); Warm = memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md (project root, chronological); Durable facts = Mem0 (cross-surface); Durable long-form = Supermemory (cross-surface). Writes happen BEFORE responding (write-ahead log).
mem0.rationale: Defines how memory should be handled across all Greg's projects. Canonical reference is in his ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

mem0.text: Greg's UI design taste: iOS 26 / visionOS liquid-glass aesthetic — real backdrop-blur, translucent layered cards, phase-tinted ambient gradients, specular highlights. Explicitly NOT generic 'glassmorphism' or flat frosted-white overlays.
mem0.rationale: Repeatedly reinforced design taste; applies beyond FinanceFlow to future UI projects.

mem0.text: Greg's animation preference: slow, smooth, flowing. Explicitly dislikes 'snappy', 'jerky', 'stuttery', 'fast', 'flashing' motion. Multiple iterations consistently went toward longer durations, softer springs, and direction-aware morphs.
mem0.rationale: Strong pattern across many turns. Defaults for any motion design work should lean slow/smooth.

mem0.text: Greg favors engagement design rooted in behavioral psychology — goal-gradient effect, identity formation, endowed progress, positive-only streaks, peak-end-rule celebrations. Explicitly rejects 'gimmicky' or 'cheap-feeling' rewards (no emojis as core UI, no confetti, no fireworks, no arcade-style fanfare). Rewards should feel restrained and earned.
mem0.rationale: Foundational design philosophy. Applies to any product targeting user behavior change.

mem0.text: UX philosophy Greg holds: touch-centered, intuitive navigation; minimize taps to accomplish anything; single contextual action visible at a time on a card. Hide actions until they're relevant (e.g., 'Mark complete' only appears when the goal is met).
mem0.rationale: Drives many specific UI decisions; defaults to contextual / progressive disclosure.

mem0.text: Greg's communication style: direct, iterative refinement. Per turn, he typically lists 3–5 numbered bullets of feedback — what's wrong, what to keep, what to change. Expects responses that acknowledge each point and propose a concrete fix before coding.
mem0.rationale: Shaping Claude's response format: structured replies that map 1:1 to his bullets.

mem0.text: Greg's git workflow on personal projects: develops on dev/feature branches off main; merges via PR; comfortable force-replacing main with dev if conflicts arise ('previous work on main no longer needed' was an actual statement). Standard merge commit preserves commit history; squash is not the default.
mem0.rationale: Defaults for branch handling and merge strategy.

mem0.text: FinanceFlow project: web app that tracks user progress through the r/PersonalFinance 'prime directive' flowchart. Repo: greg-maggard/FinanceFlow. Stack: Vite + React + TypeScript, Tailwind, Framer Motion, Zustand. MVP shipped May 2026 via PR #1 (merged commit 0a01d48 on main).
mem0.rationale: Foundational project context for future FinanceFlow-related conversations.

mem0.text: FinanceFlow conceptual reframe: progress bars fill as the user FUNDS / SAVES toward category goals (not as they spend). The product gamifies covering expenses through savings, not constraining spending. This is the philosophical heart of the app's behavior model.
mem0.rationale: Core product decision that should never be reverted; differentiates from typical budgeting apps.

mem0.text: FinanceFlow integrates YNAB via Personal Access Token (PAT) entered in Settings. Per-recurring-category mapping (Rent → YNAB category). Manual 'Refresh from YNAB' pulls current-month 'Budgeted' amount as 'funded' and 'goal_target' as 'target'. PAT stored in a separate persisted Zustand store (ynabStore.ts), explicitly NOT in main AppState — so JSON export/import never includes the token.
mem0.rationale: Architectural decision worth remembering: PAT segregation from exportable state.

mem0.text: FinanceFlow card action-area rules: (1) No Mark Complete or Next Step button visible until goal bar is 100%. (2) Only ONE completion-related button visible at a time (single contextual slot, fade between states). (3) Recurring tasks (Rent, Food, etc.) use monthly completion via Mark Complete — sets monthlyChecks[currentMonth], NOT the permanent completed flag. (4) Streak count shown as a small non-interactive chip in the header (no fire emoji, just '3 mos').
mem0.rationale: Hard-won UI rules from many iterations; reverting any of them would re-introduce flagged problems.

supermemory.title: Greg's Global Memory Protocol (CLAUDE.md content)
supermemory.description: Canonical Memory Architecture document Greg established in May 2026. Describes the four-layer memory system (hot SESSION-STATE.md, warm memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md, durable facts Mem0, durable long-form Supermemory), the write-ahead log protocol, cross-surface routing rules, and session-end promotion path. Originally pasted into the FinanceFlow sandbox as a one-time setup prompt.
supermemory.content:
# Global Instructions

## Memory Architecture

Four layers, each with a distinct job:

| Layer | Storage | Scope | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hot** | `SESSION-STATE.md` (project root) | Current Claude Code session | Survive context compaction |
| **Warm** | `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (project root) | Project, chronological | Local audit trail of activity |
| **Durable facts** | **Mem0** (via MCP) | Cross-surface (Claude Code, claude.ai, Cowork) | Preferences, decisions, status |
| **Durable long-form** | **Supermemory** (via MCP) | Cross-surface | Articles, PDFs, notes, reference material |

Hot + Warm are local files, Claude Code only. Mem0 + Supermemory are cloud-backed and reachable from every Claude surface (when configured as Connectors on claude.ai).

---

## Write-Ahead Log (WAL) Protocol — Hot/Warm Layers

Apply in every project. Writes happen *before* responding, not after — this is what makes them survive compaction.

### On session start
1. If `SESSION-STATE.md` exists in the project root, read it first.
2. If today's `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` exists, skim it.
3. If neither exists, proceed — they'll be created when warranted. Do not ask permission, just create.

### Write to `SESSION-STATE.md` BEFORE responding when:
- The user states a concrete decision, preference, or correction.
- A task is started, paused, or completed.
- A blocker or open question surfaces.
- An architectural choice is made.

Use Edit. Keep entries terse (bullets, not prose). Update the `_Last updated:_` timestamp.

### On significant milestones
- Append a one-line entry to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` (create file/dir if missing).

### Hygiene
- When an "Active Task" completes, move the entry into the day's `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md` and clear the slot.
- Weekly: prune resolved entries from "Recent Decisions" and "Open Questions".

### What does NOT belong in SESSION-STATE.md or daily logs
- Code patterns, architecture, file paths — already in code + auto-memory.
- Long narrative — keep it scannable.
- Anything `git log` already captures.

---

## Cross-Surface Memory Routing — Durable Layers

The local WAL layer covers *this session, this project*. Mem0 and Supermemory cover *every Claude, every surface, forever*. Route deliberately.

### Mem0 — preferences, decisions, facts

Save to Mem0 when something is:
- A durable fact about the user (role, goals, constraints, identity)
- A preference or working style
- A decision or rule
- A status update that may change over time
- Feedback or correction Claude should remember

Rule of thumb: **if it fits on one line and could be relevant in a future conversation on any topic → Mem0.**

Search Mem0 on every meaningful turn — it's atomic and token-cheap.

### Supermemory — long-form content

Save to Supermemory when something is:
- An article, PDF, or document worth preserving verbatim
- A long-form note, journal entry, or planning doc
- A research write-up, methodology, or reference material
- A great conversation worth keeping in full

Rule of thumb: **if it's multi-paragraph content you want preserved with source intact → Supermemory.**

Search Supermemory only when the conversation references stored material, or the user asks Claude to consult "your notes" / "what we saved about X". Don't search by default — chunks are large and noisy.

### Collision rule

When something could go either way, ask: *do I want Claude to recall the fact, or the source?*
- Fact about what I'm doing → Mem0
- The source document itself → Supermemory

Both layers can hold related entries — Mem0 the summary fact, Supermemory the source document.

---

## Session-End Promotion Path

When closing out a session or hitting a meaningful milestone:

1. **Local archive**: Append the day's events to `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`.
2. **Durable fact?** → Save to Mem0.
3. **Long-form content produced or referenced?** → Save to Supermemory.
4. **`SESSION-STATE.md`**: Keep only what's still active. Move resolved items to the daily log.

Do not duplicate aggressively. A decision saved to Mem0 doesn't need to be restated in `SESSION-STATE.md`.

---

## Memory Discipline

- **Don't save what code or `git log` already tells you.**
- **Don't save ephemeral state to durable layers.**
- **Update beats append.** When a fact changes, update the existing memory.
- **Verify before citing.** Memories are point-in-time — confirm before acting on a recalled fact.
